newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss UBP sees gold heading toward $350.
newsitem.headline: Swiss UBP sees gold heading toward $350.

text.p: Switzerland's Union Bancaire Privee said it expected gold prices to slide back toward $350 an ounce as its traditional role as guarantor of currencies' value is eroded by Europe's single currency project.

"Gold is 9.5 percent off its annual peak and should continue to drop back towards $350, compared with $378 at the end of September," it said in its latest review of commodities. Gold was trading today around $383.70/$384.00.
Rather than providing a safe haven for investors worried the new Euro currency will be weak when launched in 1999, gold was being hit hard by the plan for economic and monetary union.

"This is because the metal reserves held by central banks will lose their purpose somewhat. Hitherto, they guaranteed the value of a national currency in the face of fluctuations, including against other European currencies," it said.
"Once exchange-rate parities are fixed at the beginning of 1999, gold's role will become less significant," it added.

The future European central bank should be able to manage the Euro's external parity with fewer resources than individual central banks do today, "and the shadow of this surplus is already overhanging the market", it said.
The International Monetary Fund was also planning to reduce its reserves, adding to bearish sentiment, it added.
